text:
maria: Heads up — observed a ~12% regression in median token TTFT on prod-rt pool after last deploy. p95 is ~30% higher. Quick triage shows more tokens taking the microkernel path even when kv cache reports a hit. Also an uptick in single-token inflight batches.

alex: Do you have an example trace or a query we can run?

maria: PromQL I used for initial check (staging/prod):
```
sum by(kernel, kv_hit) (rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m]))
```
Then I computed TTFT from token_latency_seconds_sum / token_latency_seconds_count grouped by kernel+kv_hit.

sam: Hmm. If kv_hit==true but kernel==microkernel, that could indicate prefetch disabled or kernel selector falling back because batch size==1. Any kernel_choice histogram?

maria: Pasted a tiny sample from canary tracer: kernel_choice histogram (counts):
- optimized-kernel: 7400
- microkernel: 2100
- fallback-emu: 120
Of the 2100 microkernel hits, ~40% had kv_hit=true.

jen: I pushed a lightweight per-token "path tag" probe to canary yesterday that emits: kernel, kv_hit, inflight_batch_size. For /routes/chat-prd we saw ~18% tokens labeled kv_hit=true but inflight_batch_size==1 => microkernel. Prefetch wasn't enabled for singletons.

alex: We need two things: 1) add these per-token labels to the token-level latency dashboard, 2) sample a small fraction (0.1%) of full traces with kernel+kv_hit to validate attribution. Watch cardinality.

maria: Proposal: expose metric labels: kernel=<string>, kv_hit=true|false, batch_bucket=one|2-4|5-16|17plus. Also record scheduler_wait_seconds, kvcache_lookup_seconds, kernel_exec_seconds. Then build a waterfall TTFT viz.

sam: Important: current "decode" time sometimes includes kvcache lookup because it's in the same timer. We should split timers so attribution is explicit: scheduler_wait | kvcache_lookup | kernel_exec | postproc. Otherwise attribution will be fuzzy when kernel selection/timing changes.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 2026-03-18T10:03 by jen completed :white_check_mark:

jen: FYI I've landed the get-probe branch that emits inflight_batch_size (sampled). Validating in staging now, saw no noticeable perf overhead at 0.1% sample.

alex: For dashboarding: if you add batch_bucket as suggested, cardinality stays low. Also add a heatmap that shows kernel choice vs batch_bucket vs kv_hit for top routes. I can take ownership of the dashboard widgets.

maria: Good. I'll open an RFC: include metric names, label schema, sampling rate, and a small PromQL primer. Tentative owners: alex -> dashboard, jen -> runtime probe, maria -> sampling and alerting config.

sam: Can we also add a nightly job that diffs token path distribution vs baseline and alerts on shift > X%? That would catch silent regressions.

maria: Agree. I'll add a detection job under Optimize alerting. Also will add a small gated canary that forces prefetch-on for singletons for one host to validate improvement.

alex: One more note — when we compute unit economics per-route, we should derive cost attribution per token path (kernel+kv_hit) so we can see where microkernel traffic is burning tokens.

jen: I'll wire a small telemetry flag to record kernel_id (hashed) for sampled tokens to help correlate with model/quantization variants.

maria: Thanks. Next steps: I will draft RFC + sample queries and drop the link here. If anyone has objections to the label names, call them out now. Otherwise I'll proceed with low-cardinality buckets. :thumbsup:

alex: LGTM.

sam: +1.

jen: +1, will monitor staging metrics later today.

maria: Linking the first quick query I'll add to the RFC so we can reproduce:
```
# median TTFT by path
histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by(le, kernel, batch_bucket, kv_hit) (rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])))
```
Will add waterfall breakdown using scheduler_wait_seconds and kvcache_lookup_seconds.

maria: Thanks all — updating RFC and will ping when dashboards are live.
